glosses: Completely destroyed or erased; effaced, obliterated.

examples.text: [G]o to the herald's office, […] and thou shalt find in that office as many records of attainted families, and escheated families, and impoverished and forgotten, and obliterate families, as of families newly erected and presently celebrated.

examples.text: [H]e [Pope Gregory I] deſigned to obliterate and extinguiſh the memorie of Heathen antiquitie and Authors.

This opinion ſeemeth to me, to leave very little or no place for the Chriſtian Religion. For […] It obliterateth the notion of Gods Holineſs, vvhich to be no Holineſs, but a common or indifferent thing.

All tenderness for the feelings of others, all selfrespect, all sense of the becoming, were obliterated from his [George Jeffreys, 1st Baron Jeffreys's] mind.

That is what distance does for us; the harsh and bitter feelings of this or that experience are slowly obliterated, and memory begins to look kindly on the past.
The seal of Pepi is in the House of Rurutȧ. The god who obliterateth sin, Ȧṭer-ȧsfet, obliterateth the transgressions which belong to Pepi in the presence of Khenti-merti in Sekhem.

examples.text: The rainclouds obliterated the sun as they swept across the sky.
Likevviſe the fragrancy of euery greene herbe yeeldeth ſuch a ſauour, as doth not a little obliterate and ouerſvvay the ſauour of the beaſt: […]

glosses: To make (a drawing, text which is printed or written, etc.) indecipherable, either by erasing or obscuring it; to blot out, to efface, to delete.

examples.text: The Senate approuing all that vvas done, decreed that his name ſhould bee obliterated out of all monuments in Rome, and neuer any Antoninus (a name before very gratious) ſhould rule againe their Empire: ſo odious vvas the remembrance of this Image of Ignominy.

As vvhen a name lodg'd in the memory, / But yet through time almoſt obliterate, / Confuſely hovers near the phantaſie: / The man that's thus affected bids relate / A catologue of names.
Becauſe our Conſcience is ſprinkled by the blood of Chriſt, vvhich defaceth and obliterateth all thoſe black Items, that othervviſe vvould be continually calling upon us.
Blessed art thou, O Lord, universal King! who pardonest and forgivest our sins, and the sins of thy people Israel, and obliteratest our guilt year after year; […]

translations.source_sense_description: to destroy (someone or something) completely, leaving no trace

glosses: Hacer que desaparezca lo escrito, trazado o pintado con una goma, borrador u otro material.

examples.text: Leído lo último que escribí, me han dado intenciones de borrarlo, pues si los conceptos de Eufrasia me resultan hermosos y sinceros, como producto inmediato de la realidad, los míos se me antojan artificiosos y de poco fuste

glosses: Tachar lo escrito para indicar que no es válido.
Hacer que algo desaparezca.

examples.text: La dicha no consiguió borrar en el espíritu de Marius otras preocupaciones

glosses: Desaparecer el recuerdo de algo.

examples.text: Quiero borrar de mi imaginación la lúgubre escena; pero pasa una noche y otra, y la escena no se borra

translations.source_sense_description: to destroy (someone or something) completely, leaving no trace

glosses: Deshacer, dejar en nada algo ya hecho.

examples.text: Destruir un argumento.

glosses: Convertir algo material en polvo, cenizas, humo o pedazos de cualquier tamaño, mediante el uso de una fuerza material y de una acción violenta.

examples.text: Un terremoto destruye una ciudad.

translations.source_sense_description: to destroy (someone or something) completely, leaving no trace

glosses: Mover algo de un lugar a otro.
Quitar o retirar un inconveniente.
Quitar a alguien de sus actividades laborales.
Tratar de nuevo un asunto que estaba olvidado o apartado de la actualidad.
Sacar de la inmovilidad, de la quietud.
Tratar un asunto con el objetivo de encontrar información relevante o cierta.
wegvagen, vernietigen

examples.text: It has been 65 years that Hiroshima was obliterated.
examples.translation: Het is 65 jaar geleden dat Hiroshima werd weggevaagd.

glosses: zetrzeć z powierzchni ziemi, zniszczyć, wymazać

examples.text: Throughout history, many words have changed their meanings and many have been completely obliterated.
examples.translation: Historycznie wiele słów zmieniło swoje znaczenie i wiele zostało kompletnie startych z powierzchni ziemi.

glosses: Effacer.

examples.text: The marks on the sheet obliterated the handwriting underneath.

glosses: Anéantir.

examples.text: The bombing campaign obliterated the city.

glosses: cancellare
odstranit, vymazat, zničit
bránit (čemu)
